title: अंश ५ · अध्याय ३

items.text:
एवं संस्तूयमाना सा देवैर्दैवमधारयत् ।
गर्भेण पुण्डरीकाक्षं जगतस्त्राणकारणम् ।। ५-३-१ ।।
items.tr:
evaṃ saṃstūyamānā sā devairdaivamadhārayat |
garbheṇa puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ jagatastrāṇakāraṇam || 5-3-1 ||

items.text:
ततोऽखिलजगत्पद्मबोधायाच्युतभान्ना ।
देवकीपूर्व्वसन्ध्यायामाविर्भूतं महात्मना ।। ५-३-२ ।।
items.tr:
tato'khilajagatpadmabodhāyācyutabhānnā |
devakīpūrvvasandhyāyāmāvirbhūtaṃ mahātmanā || 5-3-2 ||

items.text:
तज्जन्मदिनमत्यर्थमाह्लाद्यमलदिङूमुखम् ।
बभूव सर्वलोकस्य कौमुदी शशिनो यथा ।। ५-३-३ ।।
items.tr:
tajjanmadinamatyarthamāhlādyamaladiṅūmukham |
babhūva sarvalokasya kaumudī śaśino yathā || 5-3-3 ||

items.text:
सन्तः सन्तोषमधिकं प्रशमं चण्डमारुतः ।
प्रसादं निम्रगा याता जायमाने जनार्दृने ।। ५-३-४ ।।
items.tr:
santaḥ santoṣamadhikaṃ praśamaṃ caṇḍamārutaḥ |
prasādaṃ nimragā yātā jāyamāne janārdṛne || 5-3-4 ||

items.text:
सिन्धवो निजशब्देन वाद्य चक्त र्मनोहरम् ।
जगुर्गन्धर्व्वपतयो ननृतुश्वाप्सरोगणाः ।। ५-३-५ ।।
items.tr:
sindhavo nijaśabdena vādya cakta rmanoharam |
jagurgandharvvapatayo nanṛtuśvāpsarogaṇāḥ || 5-3-5 ||

items.text:
ससृजुः पुष्पवर्षाणि देवा भुव्यन्तरीक्षगाः ।
जज्वलुश्वाग्रयः शान्ता जायमाने जनार्द्दने ।। ५-३-६ ।।
items.tr:
sasṛjuḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi devā bhuvyantarīkṣagāḥ |
jajvaluśvāgrayaḥ śāntā jāyamāne janārddane || 5-3-6 ||

items.text:
मध्यरात्रेऽखिलाधारे जायमाने जनार्दने ।
मन्द्र जगर्ज्जुर्जलदाः पूष्पचवृष्टिचो द्रिच ।। ५-३-७ ।।
items.tr:
madhyarātre'khilādhāre jāyamāne janārdane |
mandra jagarjjurjaladāḥ pūṣpacavṛṣṭico drica || 5-3-7 ||

items.text:
फुल्लेन्दीवरपत्राभं चतुर्बीहुमुदीक्ष्य तम् ।
श्रीवत्सवक्षसं जातं तुष्टावानकदुन्दुभिः ।। ५-३-८ ।।
items.tr:
phullendīvarapatrābhaṃ caturbīhumudīkṣya tam |
śrīvatsavakṣasaṃ jātaṃ tuṣṭāvānakadundubhiḥ || 5-3-8 ||

items.text:
अभिष्टूय च तं वागभिः प्रसन्नप्तभिर्महामतिः ।
विज्ञापयामास तदा कंसाद्भीतो द्रिजोत्तम ।। ५-३-९ ।।
items.tr:
abhiṣṭūya ca taṃ vāgabhiḥ prasannaptabhirmahāmatiḥ |
vijñāpayāmāsa tadā kaṃsādbhīto drijottama || 5-3-9 ||

items.text:
ज्ञातोऽसि देवदेवेश । शचङ्ख-चक्र-गदाधर ।
दिव्यरूपमिदं देव प्रसादेनोपसंहर ।। ५-३-१० ।।
items.tr:
jñāto'si devadeveśa | śacaṅkha-cakra-gadādhara |
divyarūpamidaṃ deva prasādenopasaṃhara || 5-3-10 ||

items.text:
अद्यवै देव । कंसोऽयं कुरुते मम घातनम् ।
अवतीर्ण इति ज्ञात्वा त्वमस्मिन मम मन्दिरे ।। ५-३-११ ।।
items.tr:
adyavai deva | kaṃso'yaṃ kurute mama ghātanam |
avatīrṇa iti jñātvā tvamasmina mama mandire || 5-3-11 ||

items.text:
योऽनन्तरूपोऽखिलविशरूपो गर्भेषु लोकान् वपुषा बिभर्त्ति ।
प्रसीदतामेष स देवदेवः स्वमाययावुष्कृतबालरूपः ।। ५-३-१२ ।।
items.tr:
yo'nantarūpo'khilaviśarūpo garbheṣu lokān vapuṣā bibhartti |
prasīdatāmeṣa sa devadevaḥ svamāyayāvuṣkṛtabālarūpaḥ || 5-3-12 ||

items.text:
उपसहर सर्व्वात्मन् । रूपमेज्वतुर्भुजम् ।
जानातु मावतारं ते कंसोऽयं दितिजाधमः ।। ५-३-१३ ।।
items.tr:
upasahara sarvvātman | rūpamejvaturbhujam |
jānātu māvatāraṃ te kaṃso'yaṃ ditijādhamaḥ || 5-3-13 ||

items.text:
ततोऽहं यत् त्वया पूर्व्वं पुत्रार्थिन्या तदद्य ते ।
सफलं देवि। सञ्जातं जातोऽहं यत् तवोदरात् ।। ५-३-१४ ।।
items.tr:
tato'haṃ yat tvayā pūrvvaṃ putrārthinyā tadadya te |
saphalaṃ devi| sañjātaṃ jāto'haṃ yat tavodarāt || 5-3-14 ||

items.text:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवांस्तूष्णीं बभूव मुनिसत्तम ।
वसुदेवोऽपि तं रात्रावादाय प्रययौ बहिः ।। ५-३-१५ ।।
items.tr:
ityuktvā bhagavāṃstūṣṇīṃ babhūva munisattama |
vasudevo'pi taṃ rātrāvādāya prayayau bahiḥ || 5-3-15 ||

items.text:
मोहिताश्वाभवंस्तत्र रक्षिणो योगनिद्रया ।
मथुराद्रारपालाश्व ब्रजत्यानकदुन्दुभौ ।। ५-३-१६ ।।
items.tr:
mohitāśvābhavaṃstatra rakṣiṇo yoganidrayā |
mathurādrārapālāśva brajatyānakadundubhau || 5-3-16 ||

items.text:
वर्षतां जलदानाञ्च तोयमत्युल्वणं निशि ।
संछाद्यानुययौ शेषः फणेनानकदुन्दुभिम् ।। ५-३-१७ ।।
items.tr:
varṣatāṃ jaladānāñca toyamatyulvaṇaṃ niśi |
saṃchādyānuyayau śeṣaḥ phaṇenānakadundubhim || 5-3-17 ||

items.text:
यमुनां चातिगम्भीरां नानावर्त्तसमाकुलाम् ।
वसुदेवो वहन् विष्णु जानुमात्रबहां ययौ ।। ५-३-१८ ।।
items.tr:
yamunāṃ cātigambhīrāṃ nānāvarttasamākulām |
vasudevo vahan viṣṇu jānumātrabahāṃ yayau || 5-3-18 ||

items.text:
कंसस्य करमादाय तत्रेवाभ्यागतांस्तटे ।
नन्दादीन् गोपवृन्दांश्व यमुनाया ददर्श सः ।। ५-३-१९ ।।
items.tr:
kaṃsasya karamādāya tatrevābhyāgatāṃstaṭe |
nandādīn gopavṛndāṃśva yamunāyā dadarśa saḥ || 5-3-19 ||

items.text:
तस्मिन् काले यशोदापि मोहिता योगनिद्रया ।
तामेव कन्यां मैत्रेय । प्रसूता मोहिते जने ।। ५-३-२० ।।
items.tr:
tasmin kāle yaśodāpi mohitā yoganidrayā |
tāmeva kanyāṃ maitreya | prasūtā mohite jane || 5-3-20 ||

items.text:
वसुदेवोऽपि विन्यस्य बालमादाय दारिकाम् ।
यसोदाशायने तुर्णमाजगामामितद्यु तिः ।। ५-३-२१ ।।
items.tr:
vasudevo'pi vinyasya bālamādāya dārikām |
yasodāśāyane turṇamājagāmāmitadyu tiḥ || 5-3-21 ||

items.text:
ददृशे च प्रबुद्धा सा यशोदा जातमात्मजम् ।
नीलोतूपलदलश्यामं ततोऽत्यर्थं मुदं ययौ ।। ५-३-२२ ।।
items.tr:
dadṛśe ca prabuddhā sā yaśodā jātamātmajam |
nīlotūpaladalaśyāmaṃ tato'tyarthaṃ mudaṃ yayau || 5-3-22 ||

items.text:
आदाय वसुदेवोऽपि दारिकां निजमन्दिरम् ।
देवकीशयने न्यस्य यथापूर्व्वमतिष्ठत ।। ५-३-२३ ।।
items.tr:
ādāya vasudevo'pi dārikāṃ nijamandiram |
devakīśayane nyasya yathāpūrvvamatiṣṭhata || 5-3-23 ||

items.text:
ततो बालध्वनिं श्रुत्वा रक्षिणः सहसोत्थिताः ।
कंसायावेदयामासुर्देवकीप्रसवं द्रिज ।। ५-३-२४ ।।
items.tr:
tato bāladhvaniṃ śrutvā rakṣiṇaḥ sahasotthitāḥ |
kaṃsāyāvedayāmāsurdevakīprasavaṃ drija || 5-3-24 ||

items.text:
कंसस्तूर्णमुपेत्यैनां ततो जग्राह बालिकाम् ।
मुञ्च मुञ्चति देवक्या सन्नकण्ठया निवारितः ।। ५-३-२५ ।।
items.tr:
kaṃsastūrṇamupetyaināṃ tato jagrāha bālikām |
muñca muñcati devakyā sannakaṇṭhayā nivāritaḥ || 5-3-25 ||

items.text:
चिक्षेप च शिलापृष्ठे सा क्षिप्ता वियति स्थितिम् ।
अवाप रूपञ्च महत् सायुधाष्टमहाभुजम् ।। ५-३-२६ ।।
items.tr:
cikṣepa ca śilāpṛṣṭhe sā kṣiptā viyati sthitim |
avāpa rūpañca mahat sāyudhāṣṭamahābhujam || 5-3-26 ||

items.text:
प्रजहास तथैवोच्चैः कंसञ्च रुषिताब्रवीत् ।
किं मया क्षिप्तया मूढ़!जातो यस्तवां वधिष्यति ।। ५-३-२७ ।।
items.tr:
prajahāsa tathaivoccaiḥ kaṃsañca ruṣitābravīt |
kiṃ mayā kṣiptayā mūṛha!jāto yastavāṃ vadhiṣyati || 5-3-27 ||

items.text:
सर्व्वस्वभूतो देवानामासीन्मृत्युः पुरा स ते ।
तदेतत् सम्प्रधार्य्याशु क्रियतां हितमात्मनः ।। ५-३-२८ ।।
items.tr:
sarvvasvabhūto devānāmāsīnmṛtyuḥ purā sa te |
tadetat sampradhāryyāśu kriyatāṃ hitamātmanaḥ || 5-3-28 ||

items.text:
इत्युक्त्वा प्रययौ देवी दिंव्यस्त्रगू-गन्ध-भूषणा ।
पश्यतो भोजराजस्य स्तुता सिद्धैर्विहायसि ।। ५-३-२९ ।।
items.tr:
ityuktvā prayayau devī diṃvyastragū-gandha-bhūṣaṇā |
paśyato bhojarājasya stutā siddhairvihāyasi || 5-3-29 ||

en_chapter: Parāçara said;—Being thus eulogised by the celestials; Devaki conceived in her womb the lotus-eyed deity—the saviour of the universe. The sun of Achyuta rose in the dawn of Devaki to cause the lotus-petal of the universe to expand. On the day of his birth, all the quarters were lighted up with joy and it gave delight to all people like unto the rays of the moon.

The pious obtained new delight; the strong wind were pacified and the river flowed silently when Janārddana was about to be born. The oceans made music with their murmurings, the Gandharvas began to sing and the Apsaras began to dance. At the time of Janārddana's birth the celestials, stationed in the sky, began to pour flowers and the holy fires glowed with a mild flame. At midnight, when the supporter of all was about to be born, the clouds began to emit low sounds and pour down rain of flowers.

As soon as Anakadundhubhi saw the child, looking like full-blown lotus-petals, having four arms and the mystic mark Sribatsa an his breast; he began to chant his glories in terms of love and respect and represented the fears he entertained of Kansa. Vasudeva said, "I have known thee, O sovereign lord of the celestials, O thou the holder of conch, discus and mace. Be pleased to withhold this thy celestial form, for Kansa will surely destroy me when he will know that thou hast descended in my dwelling". Devaki said,—"God of gods, who art identical with all things, in whose person all the religions of the world exist and who, by illusion, hast assumed the condition of an infant, have pity me, withold thy four-armed shape. Let not Kansa, the wicked son of Diti, know of this birth".

To this Bhagavat replied—"O worshipful dame, I was worshipped by thee before to be born as thy son. Thy prayers have now been granted and I am now born as thy son". So saying he was silent and Vasudeva, taking the babe, went out the same night. The guards and gate-keepers of Mathura were all charmed by Yoganidrā and none of them obstructed the passage of Anakadundhubhi. It was raining heavily at that time and the many-headed serpent Sesha followed Vasudeva spreading his hoods above their heads. And when he, with the child in his arms, crossed the Yamuna, deep as it was and dangerous with numerous whirlpools, the waters were silent and rose not above his knee. On the bank he saw Nanda and others who had come there to bring tribute to Kansa, but they did not see him. At that time Yasoda was also influenced by Yoganidrā, whom she had given birth as her daughter and whom the wise Vasudeva took up, placing his son in her place by the side of the mother. He then speedily came back home. When Yasoda awoke, she found she had been delivered of a boy as black as the dark lotus-leaves; and she was greatly delighted.

Vasudeva, taking the female child of Yasoda, reached his house unperceived and placed the child in the bed of Devaki. He then remained as usual. The guards were awakened by the cry of the new-born babe and starting up they informed Kansa that Devaki had given birth to a child. Kansa immediately went to the house of Vasudeva where he got hold of the infant. Devaki faintingly prevented him, crying out again and again—"Do not destroy it! Do not destroy it". Kansa dashed it against a stone; it at once went up to the sky and expanded into a gigantic figure, having eight arms each bearing a formidable weapon. This terrible figure laughed and said to Kansa. "What benefit have you derived, O Kansa, by hurling me to the ground? He is born who shall destroy thee, the mighty one amongst celestials, who was formerly the destroyer, Considering this do thou accomplish what shall tend to thy welfare". Having said this, the goddess, decorated with heavenly unguents and garlands, and glorified by the spirits of the air, disappeared from the sight of the king of the Bhojas.
